page: Amazon Web Services r7a.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by 4 dedicated x86_64 cores from an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. Governed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 1 thread per physical core without simultaneous multithreading overhead. Memory configuration consists of 32.0 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector instruction support includes AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions, alongside cryptographic accelerations including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark measurements show strong single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core reaching 1974.0 and stress-ng single-core achieving 3077.67, placing both metrics in the upper quartile. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput is also strong at 13.9 GB/sec. Across multi-core metrics, performance settles into the median range, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6300.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 10555.37. Uncached memory read bandwidth over large 256 MB blocks shows a lower-tier result at 37.49 GB/sec, whereas cached block reads sustain 592.0 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration omits local disk storage, requiring external EBS network-attached storage over an instance baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. There is no bundled GPU acceleration, which is reflected in restricted throughput for larger language model inference tasks, such as 7B model generation at 8.53 tokens per second. However, Redis operations register at 10.46 million operations per second.

Cost efficiency is concentrated in memory density, providing high DDR5 capacity per compute unit without requiring licensing or provisioning for higher core counts. The instance is suited for in-memory caches, distributed key-value datastores, medium-scale relational databases, and enterprise applications requiring high RAM-to-vCPU ratios without high sustained local I/O requirements.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 32.0 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory, delivering a generous 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Instruction set features include AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic hardware acceleration. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached volumes and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks reveal strong single-core execution alongside median multi-core and memory throughput. Supported by 10.46 million Redis SET operations per second, r7a.xlarge delivers cost-efficient memory scaling for memory-bound workloads such as caching layers, in-memory key-value stores, and database engines.
